name: Specialization & Elite Mastery Loop
description: An end-to-end RPG build-and-challenge loop: level growth and durable specialization selections unlock gated skill ranks and active abilities; ordinary respecs rebuild ranks without erasing identity or earned mastery. Finite elite encounters combine level scaling with deterministic enemy affixes, timed and interruptible telegraphs, ordinary damage resolution, and stable defeat metadata. The same defeat can advance the encounter, character XP, mastery, and existing loot owners without any one of them owning another's state. Encounter completion can grant deduplicated mastery, while completed changes restore through their owners. All identities, skills, affixes, attacks, encounters, items, UI, and balance tables remain host supplied.

acceptanceCriteria: Legacy skill nodes and ability catalog entries without specialization or mastery fields retain their previous purchase, assignment, restore, and respec behavior.

A new specialization selection succeeds only when level, required skill ranks, specialization prerequisites, exclusivity, capacity, and replacement rules all pass; rejection changes no selection or bonus state.
Restored specializations, mastery XP, credit ids, affix assignments, encounter ledgers, and telegraph timers do not emit historical selection, rank, spawn, completion, or hit events.
A specialization-gated skill checks the active identity only for new purchases; restored ranks are not deleted by edited gates, and an ordinary Build Respec preserves both specialization and mastery.

Mastery credits only matching completed facts from active tracks, derives ranks from strictly increasing thresholds, and never credits the same track twice for one stable cast, defeat, quest, or encounter completion id.
Ability Loadout requires every declared source-rank, specialization, mastery, slot, and duplicate rule before assignment, and publishes one complete kit after any gate changes.
Elite Affixes reproduces the same legal set from the same seed and stable ids, includes prerequisite closure, enforces exclusions and threat bands, and returns restored assignments without rerolling.

Elite Encounter Director combines level scaling and affix multipliers once at spawn, uses stable unit ids, and preserves encounter, wave, tier, and affix metadata through Damage Resolver's entityDefeated event.

A wave advances only after every unit spawned for that wave has a matching defeat; the final wave emits one completion id, and allowReplay=false rejects another start or encounter-level mastery credit.
Player-team elimination fails rather than completes the encounter, and reset removes living units through unitRemoved without XP, loot, mastery, or a false defeat.

Elite Telegraph Scheduler reads the current Aggro Table target at windup, locks it for that telegraph, waits a positive readable windup, and emits at most one attackCommitted plus one ordinary combat.hit.
Declared interrupt effects, caster defeat, locked-target defeat, missing targets, and encounter reset cancel the windup and emit no hit; cancellation never becomes damage or loot.
Intent Marks can be removed without changing aggro, cooldowns, windups, hits, encounters, mastery, or rewards; with it present, every committed or cancelled telegraph leaves the projection.
Damage Resolver remains the only final-damage owner for player and elite attacks, and Status Effects remains the only timed-effect ledger.
Drop Director alone decides drop eligibility and quantity, Affix Loot Generator rolls only accepted requests in onRequest mode, and Slotted Bag or Core Inventory retains item-capacity authority.
One elite defeat may independently advance its encounter, character XP, mastery, and loot, but none of those consumers may duplicate or synthesize another consumer's completed event.
Rejected specialization choices, duplicate mastery facts, invalid affix assignments, stale defeats, and cancelled telegraphs emit no completed-change save trigger.

Removing Specialization, Mastery, and all content gated by them leaves legacy buildcraft and elite combat functional; removing the elite slice leaves build planning and usage-based mastery from other declared sources functional.
Identical content, seeds, restored state, target selections, timer inputs, and stable event ids reproduce selections, ranks, affixes, waves, telegraphs, hits, rewards, and saves deterministically.
